for: Mistral Vibe Work, scheduled tasks and Chat

prompts.name: ai-use-case-intake
prompts.summary: Turn a proposed AI use case into a structured intake record, with the unanswered governance questions listed as questions.
prompts.use_when: Use when someone proposes an AI use case and you need it written down in a comparable shape before anyone assesses it.
inputs: The proposal, thread or meeting note describing the use case
Your own intake template, if you have one
prompts.outputs: An intake record with purpose, data, decision impact, human role and reversibility, plus Unanswered questions routed to named owners.

prompts.name: change-announcement-draft
prompts.summary: Draft an internal announcement for a change, with the questions people will ask answered or explicitly listed as unanswered.
prompts.use_when: Use when a change is about to affect colleagues and you need an announcement that survives the first ten replies.
inputs: The change description, dates and affected population
Any support, training or FAQ material that already exists
prompts.outputs: A draft announcement plus an Anticipated questions list split into answered and unanswered, and a What I invented check.

prompts.name: claim-check-pack
prompts.summary: Check the factual claims in a piece of writing one by one and return supported, contradicted, mixed or not found with sources.
prompts.use_when: Use when something is about to be published or sent and you need each factual claim checked against a source rather than read for tone.
inputs: The draft text, document or post
Web search
prompts.outputs: One row per claim with a verdict, the source URL, the date on that page, and a separate list of claims that cannot be checked.

prompts.name: contract-renewal-risk-read
prompts.summary: Read a contract before a renewal and return the dates, the money, the exits and the clauses that move without you.
prompts.use_when: Use when a contract is coming up for renewal and you need the mechanical terms in front of you before any conversation with the vendor.
inputs: The contract, and any amendment or order form attached to it
prompts.outputs: A table of the mechanical terms with clause references, plus Automatic behaviour, Questions for the vendor, and Not in this document.

prompts.name: cost-driver-breakdown
prompts.summary: Break a cost line into its drivers from the data you supply, showing the arithmetic and refusing to guess at missing pieces.
prompts.use_when: Use when a cost has moved and you need to know which components moved, before anyone explains it in a meeting.
inputs: The cost export, invoice detail or billing report for both periods
prompts.outputs: A driver table with both periods, the delta, the share of the total move, the arithmetic shown, and an Unexplained residual line.

prompts.name: decision-log-entry
prompts.summary: Turn a thread or a set of notes into one decision log entry, with the decision quoted and the alternatives recorded.
prompts.use_when: Use when a decision has just been taken in a meeting or a thread and you need it written down before the reasoning evaporates.
inputs: The thread, notes or transcript where the decision was taken
Any document the decision refers to
prompts.outputs: A single log entry with Decision, Date and forum, Decided by, Because, Alternatives considered, Consequences, Revisit when, and Unresolved.

prompts.name: exec-update-draft
prompts.summary: Draft a short leadership update from the evidence you already have, with every claim tied to a source.
prompts.use_when: Use when you owe someone senior a written update and the material is scattered across tickets, documents and threads.
inputs: The tracker or project board
The document or deck the work produced
Any thread where the decisions were taken
prompts.outputs: A draft update under 300 words with Position, Changes, Risks, Asks, and a separate evidence list keyed to each claim.

prompts.name: inbox-triage-plan
prompts.summary: Sort an unread mailbox into what needs you, what needs a decision and what can wait, without touching a single message.
prompts.use_when: Use when you are behind on mail and need a plan for the next hour instead of a folder full of unread items.
inputs: Gmail or Outlook
prompts.outputs: Four buckets with one line per message, its ask, its deadline, and a separate list of what was unclear.

prompts.name: meeting-prep-brief
prompts.summary: Build a one page brief for a specific meeting from the invite, the thread history and the last decisions taken.
prompts.use_when: Use when you are walking into a meeting you did not organise and need the history, the open questions and the likely asks.
inputs: The calendar invite
Mail or chat threads with the attendees
Any document attached to the invite
prompts.outputs: A brief with Purpose, Who is in the room, What happened last time, Open questions, Likely asks, and What I could not find.

prompts.name: metric-definition-audit
prompts.summary: Collect every definition of a metric in use across your documents and show where they disagree.
prompts.use_when: Use when two teams report the same metric with different numbers and you need to find out whether they are measuring the same thing.
inputs: The reports, dashboards specs, documents or threads where the metric appears
prompts.outputs: One row per definition found with its source and date, a disagreement matrix, and a list of the questions the documents cannot answer.

prompts.name: policy-gap-questions
prompts.summary: Compare a policy against a framework or standard you supply and return the gaps as questions rather than as findings.
prompts.use_when: Use when you have to review an internal policy against a framework and want the gaps in a form you can take to the owner.
inputs: The policy document
The framework, standard or control set you are comparing against
prompts.outputs: A control by control table with Addressed, Partly addressed, Not found, plus quoted evidence and one question per gap.

prompts.name: regulation-change-watch
prompts.summary: Establish what a named regulation currently says on the points you care about, with the official text quoted and dated.
prompts.use_when: Use when you need the current state of a specific regulation on specific questions, and secondhand summaries are not good enough.
inputs: Web search, pointed at the official publisher
Any internal note stating what you currently believe
prompts.outputs: A question by question table quoting the official text with its identifier and date, plus Amended, Disputed and Not established.

prompts.name: reply-drafts-for-review
prompts.summary: Create unsent reply drafts for a named set of messages, one at a time, with a stated reason for each.
prompts.use_when: Use when you have triaged your mail and want the routine replies written but not sent.
inputs: Gmail, where drafting is the documented ceiling
writes: Creates draft messages in the mail client. Work asks for approval before each write.
prompts.outputs: One unsent draft per message, plus a table of what each draft commits you to and which ones were left for you to write.

prompts.name: rfp-requirement-extract
prompts.summary: Turn a tender or RFP document into a numbered requirement table with page references and an explicit list of ambiguities.
prompts.use_when: Use when a tender, RFP or statement of work arrives and you need every requirement as a row before anyone starts writing answers.
inputs: The RFP, tender or statement of work, including annexes
prompts.outputs: A numbered requirement table with page and clause references, plus Ambiguous, Conflicting, and Not a requirement.

prompts.name: risk-register-draft
prompts.summary: Turn your material into a draft risk register where every risk carries the evidence it was inferred from.
prompts.use_when: Use when you need a first risk register for a project and want it built from what people actually wrote rather than from a generic list.
inputs: Project documents, plans, threads or notes
prompts.outputs: One row per risk with its evidence quoted, its owner blank, and blank likelihood and impact cells for a human to score.

prompts.name: rollout-plan-draft
prompts.summary: Draft a staged rollout plan with entry and exit criteria per stage, and a named list of what is not yet decided.
prompts.use_when: Use when a change has to reach a population in stages and you need a first plan that makes the unknowns visible.
inputs: What is being rolled out, to whom, and by when
Any constraint document: change windows, approvals, training, licences
prompts.outputs: A stage table with entry and exit criteria, a rollback line per stage, and separate Assumptions, Dependencies and Open decisions lists.

prompts.name: spreadsheet-anomaly-read
prompts.summary: Read a spreadsheet or export and report what looks wrong in the data before anyone draws a conclusion from it.
prompts.use_when: Use when you have been handed a file to analyse and want the data quality problems surfaced before the analysis, not after.
inputs: The spreadsheet, CSV or export
prompts.outputs: A structure summary, a row per anomaly with the cells involved, and separate lists for What I assumed and What I could not check.

prompts.name: stakeholder-reframe
prompts.summary: Reframe the same material for a named audience, showing what was cut and what claim each audience is being asked to accept.
prompts.use_when: Use when one piece of work has to be told to a second audience and you want the translation visible rather than invisible.
inputs: The original material
Who the new audience is and what decision they face
prompts.outputs: The reframed piece, a table of what was cut, added or softened, and the single claim the audience must accept for it to work.

prompts.name: support-theme-synthesis
prompts.summary: Theme a batch of support tickets or feedback with counts, quoted evidence and an explicit list of what cannot be concluded.
prompts.use_when: Use when you have a pile of tickets, reviews or survey answers and need the themes with numbers rather than an impression.
inputs: The ticket export, review set or survey responses
prompts.outputs: Themed groups with record counts and shares, anonymised quotes keyed to record ids, plus Contradictions and Cannot conclude.

prompts.name: vendor-landscape-scan
prompts.summary: Scan a vendor category against criteria you set, with every claim quoted from a dated page and the gaps named.
prompts.use_when: Use when you need a first pass at who is in a market and what they claim, before anyone books a demo.
inputs: Web search
Any vendor documents or pricing pages you already hold
prompts.outputs: A vendor by criterion table where every cell carries a quote, a URL and a page date, plus Could not establish and Contradictions.

prompts.name: weekly-project-catchup
prompts.summary: Catch up on one project across mail, chat and the tracker, and separate what moved from what is stuck.
prompts.use_when: Use when you have been away from a project and need what changed, what is blocked and what needs you, before you walk into a meeting.
inputs: Gmail or Outlook
Slack
Linear, Atlassian or the tracker you use
prompts.outputs: A dated brief with What moved, What is stuck, Decisions taken, What needs you, and Not covered.

prompts.name: access-review-prep
prompts.summary: A quarterly pack that assembles who has access to what, ready for the owners to review, with no recommendation attached.
prompts.use_when: Use when access reviews stall because assembling the lists takes longer than reviewing them.
inputs: The access exports or listings, in Drive, SharePoint or a repository
prompts.outputs: Per system membership lists grouped by owner, plus flags for dormant, unmatched and unowned entries.

prompts.name: backlog-ageing-report
prompts.summary: A fortnightly read on how old the backlog is, where items sit untouched, and which ones nobody owns.
prompts.use_when: Use when the backlog keeps growing and nobody can say which parts of it are actually dead.
inputs: Linear, Atlassian or GitHub
prompts.outputs: Age distributions by bucket and by state, the oldest untouched items, and No owner and Never triaged lists.

prompts.name: competitor-watch
prompts.summary: A weekly read on a named list of competitors, restricted to what changed on their own public pages.
prompts.use_when: Use when you want a steady signal on a handful of competitors without a daily feed of commentary.
inputs: The named list of competitors and the pages that matter
prompts.outputs: One line per competitor with what changed and the link, a No change list, and a Could not check list.

prompts.name: doc-change-watch
prompts.summary: A weekly read on which documents in a named space changed, who changed them, and which ones are overdue a review.
prompts.use_when: Use when a policy or procedure space matters and nobody is watching what quietly changed in it.
inputs: Google Drive, SharePoint or Notion, and the specific space or folder
prompts.outputs: Changed documents with author and date, an Overdue review list, and a No owner list.

prompts.name: inbox-triage-digest
prompts.summary: A daily read-only digest of what arrived in your mailbox overnight, ordered by who is waiting on you.
prompts.use_when: Use when you want the state of your mailbox in one note each morning instead of opening it cold.
inputs: Gmail or Outlook
prompts.outputs: Four short buckets, the oldest unanswered ask, and a list of anything the run could not read.

prompts.name: kpi-pack-prep
prompts.summary: A monthly figures pack built only from the sources, with each number carrying its definition, period and denominator.
prompts.use_when: Use when the monthly pack takes a day to assemble and half the meeting is spent questioning the numbers.
inputs: The source exports or dashboards, in Drive, SharePoint, Notion or Stripe
prompts.outputs: One block per metric with the figure, its definition, its period and its source, plus Missing and Changed definition lists.

prompts.name: overnight-incident-digest
prompts.summary: A morning digest of what broke overnight, taken from the channels and tickets themselves, with the open questions listed.
prompts.use_when: Use when incidents are discussed across a chat tool and a tracker and you want one read before the stand-up.
inputs: Slack
Linear, Atlassian or GitHub
prompts.outputs: One block per incident with timeline, current state as stated, who is on it, and what is still unanswered.

prompts.name: pipeline-hygiene-check
prompts.summary: A weekly read on the records in your pipeline that are stale, incomplete or internally inconsistent.
prompts.use_when: Use when pipeline reviews keep turning into arguments about whether the data is right.
inputs: The pipeline source: Notion, Linear, Atlassian or an exported sheet in Drive or SharePoint
prompts.outputs: Grouped exception lists with record links and counts, plus the totals with and without the exceptions.

prompts.name: project-rollup
prompts.summary: A weekly read-only rollup across your tracker and channels, built from what moved and what did not.
prompts.use_when: Use when you write the same weekly status by hand from three tools every Friday.
inputs: Linear, Atlassian or GitHub
Slack or Notion, if decisions live there
prompts.outputs: Per workstream progress, slipped dates with old and new, items with no owner, and a Went quiet list.

prompts.name: regulation-diff-watch
prompts.summary: A weekly check of named regulator and standards pages for changes, quoted and linked, with no interpretation.
prompts.use_when: Use when a small set of official sources governs your work and you need the change before the newsletter tells you.
inputs: The named list of official pages to watch
prompts.outputs: Changed pages with quoted before and after where available, a No change list, and a Could not check list.

prompts.name: spend-anomaly-watch
prompts.summary: A weekly read on charges that moved against their own history, with the arithmetic shown and no cause attached.
prompts.use_when: Use when spend is spread across vendors and nobody notices a change until the quarter closes.
inputs: Stripe, or an export in Drive or SharePoint
prompts.outputs: Ranked changes with both figures and the difference, new and stopped charges, and what could not be compared.

prompts.name: vendor-renewal-lookahead
prompts.summary: A monthly look at contracts reaching a notice window, with the dates counted and the missing documents named.
prompts.use_when: Use when auto-renewal has already cost you once and nobody owns the calendar.
inputs: Google Drive, SharePoint or Notion, and the contract folder or register
prompts.outputs: Contracts ordered by notice deadline, the arithmetic behind each date, and lists for missing terms and missing owners.

prompts.name: analogy-check
prompts.summary: Test an analogy you are about to use by finding where it holds, where it breaks, and what a listener would wrongly conclude.
prompts.use_when: Use when you are about to build an explanation or a pitch on a comparison.
inputs: The analogy, stated as X is like Y
Who will hear it and what you want them to conclude
prompts.outputs: Where it holds, where it breaks, the wrong conclusions it invites, and two alternatives.

prompts.name: assumption-list
prompts.summary: Surface the assumptions a plan or argument rests on, ranked by what happens if each one is wrong.
prompts.use_when: Use when a plan feels solid and you want the things nobody stated written down.
inputs: The plan, argument or proposal
prompts.outputs: Stated and unstated assumptions, each with its consequence if false, ranked by damage and cheapest check.

prompts.name: error-message-decode
prompts.summary: Read an error message back in plain words, separate what it states from what it implies, and rank the causes by how cheap they are to check.
prompts.use_when: Use when an error is unfamiliar and you want the reading before you start changing things.
inputs: The error message in full, and what you were doing when it appeared
prompts.outputs: A plain reading, what the message does and does not state, ranked candidate causes with a cheap check for each.

prompts.name: explain-to-a-newcomer
prompts.summary: Explain something to a named level of prior knowledge, with the terms that have to be learned separated from the ones that can wait.
prompts.use_when: Use when you have to bring somebody up to speed and you have stopped being able to tell what is obvious.
inputs: The thing to explain
Who the newcomer is and what they already know
prompts.outputs: A layered explanation, a must-know terms list, a can-wait list, and the questions they will ask next.

prompts.name: jargon-decode
prompts.summary: Decode the unfamiliar terms in a piece of text, separating the ones with a real definition from the ones that are context dependent.
prompts.use_when: Use when you are reading something in an unfamiliar area and half the nouns are doing unknown work.
inputs: The text containing the jargon
The field it comes from, if you know it
prompts.outputs: A term table with plain meanings and confidence, a list of terms that mean different things in different places, and one plain paragraph.

prompts.name: options-table
prompts.summary: Lay out the options against criteria you name, with an evidence column that shows which cells are actually known.
prompts.use_when: Use when a choice has drifted into a conversation and nobody has written the options next to each other.
inputs: The options
The criteria that matter and what the decision is
prompts.outputs: A comparison table with an evidence basis per cell, what would change the answer, and the option that was not listed.

prompts.name: plain-english-rewrite
prompts.summary: Rewrite dense or evasive text in plain English and flag the sentences that turned out to mean nothing.
prompts.use_when: Use when a paragraph reads as important and you cannot tell what it commits anyone to.
inputs: The text to rewrite
prompts.outputs: A plain English version, a table of the terms replaced, and a list of sentences with no content.

prompts.name: pre-mortem-quick
prompts.summary: Assume the thing failed, then work backwards to the causes, the earliest visible signal and what to do now.
prompts.use_when: Use when a plan is agreed, the deadline is real, and nobody wants to reopen it.
inputs: The plan and its deadline
What success is supposed to look like
prompts.outputs: Ranked failure stories with their earliest signal, the cheapest action now, and the failure nobody is watching.

prompts.name: regex-explain
prompts.summary: Explain a regular expression piece by piece, with examples that match, examples that do not, and the cases where it will surprise you.
prompts.use_when: Use when you are about to trust a pattern somebody else wrote, or one you wrote a month ago.
inputs: The pattern, and the flavour or language if you know it
What it is supposed to match
prompts.outputs: A piece by piece reading, matching and non-matching examples, the surprises, and flavour differences.

prompts.name: second-order-effects
prompts.summary: Trace what a decision causes after the intended effect, including how people will respond to being measured by it.
prompts.use_when: Use when a change will alter what people are measured on, paid for or asked to report.
inputs: The decision and its intended effect
Who is affected and how they are currently measured
prompts.outputs: First, second and third order effects with the mechanism for each, plus gaming routes and what to watch.

prompts.name: sql-read
prompts.summary: Read a SQL query back in plain words, name what it counts, and flag the joins and filters that quietly change the answer.
prompts.use_when: Use when a number came from a query you did not write and you have to decide whether to trust it.
inputs: The query
What the number is supposed to mean
prompts.outputs: A plain reading, the grain of the result, ranked traps in the joins and filters, and the checks that would confirm it.

prompts.name: steelman-the-objection
prompts.summary: Build the strongest honest version of the argument against your position, then separate what you can answer from what you cannot.
prompts.use_when: Use when you are about to present something and every objection in your head is an easy one.
inputs: Your position and the reasoning behind it
Who will be objecting and what they care about
prompts.outputs: Three or four strong objections ranked by strength, your available answers, and the ones with no good answer.

prompts.name: subject-line-options
prompts.summary: Eight subject lines built on different angles, each with the promise it makes and what the body must then deliver.
prompts.use_when: Use when the message is written and the subject line is the part still costing you ten minutes.
inputs: What the message is about and who receives it
The action you want from the reader
prompts.outputs: Eight options across distinct angles, each with its implied promise, plus the ones that overpromise named.

prompts.name: tighten-this
prompts.summary: Cut a piece of writing to a stated length and show what was lost, so you can judge the trade rather than accept it.
prompts.use_when: Use when something you wrote is too long and you want the cut shown rather than hidden.
inputs: The text to cut
The target length
prompts.outputs: The tightened text at the target length, a list of what was cut, and anything that could not be cut without losing meaning.

prompts.name: tone-shift
prompts.summary: Move a message along one named axis of tone and show exactly which words did the work.
prompts.use_when: Use when a message is right in substance and wrong in temperature.
inputs: The text
The direction, named as an axis
prompts.outputs: The shifted version, a table of the words that changed, and a warning on any change that altered the meaning.

prompts.name: tradeoff-frame
prompts.summary: Name the real trade-off behind a decision, who pays on each side, and the conditions under which each choice is right.
prompts.use_when: Use when a discussion keeps going in circles because both sides are right about different things.
inputs: The decision and the positions people are taking
prompts.outputs: The trade-off named as two goods in tension, who bears each cost, the conditions favouring each side, and any false choice.
